lines.text: Ladies and gentlemen. Marvin the Magnificent!
Dad, it is a Tuesday. I came down for cereal.
And you shall have cereal. After the show.
Tonight's star. The family advent calendar.
Hello. Why am I out of the closet? It is November.
The calendar is right. It is the eleventh of November.
Magic does not own a calendar.
I am the calendar. Magic owns me now, apparently.
First trick. Zoe, pick a door. Any door.
Door seven.
Remember that number. Now look behind your ear.
There is a chocolate behind my ear. It is warm.
It has been there since lunch. That is called preparation.
It is melted into my hair, Dad.
And that is a bell. Door seven is a bell.
Second trick. I will make the calendar float.
You are holding it with your other hand.
That is my magic hand. It does not count.
Abracadabra. Behold. Floating.
I am on the fridge. You stuck me to the fridge with a magnet.
The magnet is shaped like a pineapple.
A magician never reveals his fruit.
Can I eat cereal now?
Not yet. The next trick needs a volunteer. And a saw.
No. Absolutely not. I am cardboard. I am mostly feelings.
Relax. It is a bread knife. Very gentle.
That is worse. Bread knives have teeth.
Fine. Third trick. The disappearing chocolate.
I open door one. And the chocolate is gone.
Whoa. Okay. That was a little good.
Door two. Also gone. Door three. Gone.
Wait. Open all of them.
A magician only opens three doors per show.
They are all empty. All twenty four. I feel very light.
Dad. When did you buy this calendar?
October third. A man has to rehearse.
He rehearsed every night at eleven.
The chocolate disappears. Into his face.
You ate the whole calendar before December!
I ate a calendar's worth of practice. Big difference.
He also hides the wrappers in the toaster.
That is why the toast smells like Christmas!
That smell is called festive. You are welcome.
Okay. My turn. And for my final trick.
No hat, no magic. Everybody knows that.
I open the vegetable drawer. The one place you never look.
And behold. A second advent calendar. Still full.
A backup. With all the doors closed. She is a genius.
How long has that been in there?
Since last year. I know you.
Behind the celery? That is dark magic.
Twenty four new doors. Good luck, Marvin.
This one stays in my room. With a lock. And a bell.
Fine. Then for my real final trick.
If you make the cereal disappear, I am leaving.
I will make myself disappear. To the store.
Get the one with fifty doors. You will need the practice.
And buy cereal. You made that disappear on Sunday.
Marvin the Magnificent, everybody. Tips go in the toaster.
